newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ex-Carrian boss Tan gets three years for HK fraud.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Carrian boss Tan gets three years for HK fraud.

text.p: The former head of the Carrian group, once one of Hong Kong's biggest corporate empires, was sentenced to three years in prison for fraud on Friday, but a huge legal bill was waived.

George Tan, 62, pleaded guilty last week to two counts of conspiracy to defraud in connection with HK$1.8 billion (US$238 million) in secret loans from the Malaysian bank, Bumiputra Malaysia Finance Ltd, in the early 1980s.
The court also issued an order during sentencing on Friday disqualifying Tan from being a company director for five years.
He was not ordered to pay the HK$200 million (US$25.6 million) that authorities have spent on investigations and court expenses in the British colony's longest and costliest trial.
Tan's defence lawyers had consistently expressed concern during the trial about his health, calling in three medical experts to testify to his heart condition and dementia.
Tan's Carrian group, which had diverse interests including property, shipping and restaurants, collapsed in 1983 under a mountain of debt.

Tan and his company stormed on to the Hong Kong scene in the early 1980s with a series of spectacular property deals. By the end of 1981, Carrian was the seventh-biggest company in Hong Kong. Its 1983 collapse was the territory's biggest corporate crash.
